lacuna.name: attention-gemm-tile-fusion
lacuna.repo_anchor: Constraint frame (the anchor, quoted): owned "paged-split decode-attention kernel scores 41.2 tok/s vs the TRITON baseline 50.1 at ctx2048; the gap is ~4.3 ms of a 24.3 ms step while attention's KV traffic is only ~0.12 ms at the DRAM wall. The residual is STRUCTURE (split-softmax workspace round-trip to DRAM, a second combine launch, step serialization), not bandwidth." The consumers downstream of attention are "W4A16 Marlin GEMMs streaming ~9 GiB/step/rank" on "TU102 / sm_75 (Turing), no cp.async, no TMA, no clusters, 2-resident-CTA occupancy law, conflicted STS halves, 535 GB/s DRAM ceiling, CUDA 13.3". Falsified levers to respect: "bandwidth levers falsified, half2 staging NO_DIFF in-engine, KV pipelining NEGATIVE". Sibling record gdn-step-coupling.json (2026-09-14) banks plan/0010-last-fifth #step-profile as the gap ledger this item's gate-1 cull reads.
lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15. The 2025-2026 published line has converged on exactly this fusion boundary, all on post-Turing hardware. (1) ClusterFusion (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv 2508.18850, Luo et al.; code xinhao-luo/ClusterFusion) fuses QKV projection + attention + output projection into ONE kernel using Hopper thread-block clusters and structured intra-cluster (DSMEM) communication as a cluster-centric dataflow; its follow-up ClusterFusion++ (arXiv 2604.23553, 2026-04) extends cluster-level fusion to the FULL transformer block during decode. Requires clusters -> sm_90+ only. (2) CODA (arXiv 2605.19269, v1 2026-05-19; Guo, Zhang, Menon, Guessous, Thakkar, Kim, Dao) reparameterizes the memory-bound ops around GEMMs (norms, residuals, reductions) to execute in the GEMM epilogue 'while a GEMM output tile remains on chip', via a fixed mainloop plus composable epilogue primitives; covers 'nearly all non-attention computation' of fwd+bwd — training-focused, but it is the CUTLASS-aligned (Thakkar, NVIDIA CUTLASS; Tri Dao) statement of epilogue-side fusion. (3) FlashMLA (DeepSeek, open-sourced 2025-02, Hopper/H800) and DeepGEMM (FP8 GEMM, 2025-02) are the MLA-decode + GEMM dataflow references — note FlashMLA issue #61 records that even on Hopper it loads via SM80-style cp.async rather than TMA, i.e. the winning pipeline is cp.async-class, not TMA-bound; sm_80 floor nonetheless. (4) Synchronization precedent that predates all of it: CUTLASS split-K reduction by semaphore (CUTLASS 'Efficient GEMM' docs: parallel reduction across CTAs via semaphores; NVIDIA/cutlass discussion #317: 'one is using semaphore, the other is using atomic add. Semaphore can guarantee deterministic results. Atomic add is faster') — the in-kernel cross-CTA combine, arch-independent back to sm_70; the CUDA threadFenceReduction sample is the canonical last-CTA-combines pattern. (5) Warp specialization: ergonomic producer/consumer warps date to Volta named barriers (bar.sync with warp counts) and became the default CUTLASS pattern at Ampere (CUTLASS 2.x multi-stage cp.async pipelines; Colfax GEMM-pipelining tutorial; PyTorch blog on Hopper ping-pong scheduling is the sm_90 evolution). On sm_75 there is no cp.async/mbarrier, so producer/consumer sync is named barriers + volatile/exlicit smem within a CTA, and global atomics + __threadfence across CTAs — strictly weaker but sufficient for a once-per-step boundary. (6) The no-fusion alternative that removes the same round trip numerically: FlashDecoding++ (arXiv 2311.01282, 2023-11; MLSys 2024, Hong et al., cited 83+) computes partial softmax against a pre-agreed 'unified max' so splits are independently normalizable and need no cross-split synchronization pass at all — synchronization-free decode softmax, plus flat-GEMM co-design. (7) Engine-side precedent: vLLM's AttnQuantFusionPass (RFC #16220; docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/design/fusions/) fuses attention-output quantization INTO the attention kernel, 'eliminating a full-precision memory round-trip of the attention output' — production proof that attention-output consumers get pulled into the attention kernel when profitable. (8) LeanAttention (arXiv 2405.10480; MLSys 2025) shows the persistent-kernel path alone does NOT remove the combine: it still runs a separate log-sum-exp combine kernel after its stream-K-style partials.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers to sm_75: (a) the semaphore/atomic in-kernel combine (threadFenceReduction / CUTLASS split-K) — pure CUDA, no sm_80 dependency; it deletes the second combine launch and converts the split-softmax workspace round-trip into an L2-resident read (TU102 ~6 MB L2 swallows a 24 heads x 8 seq x 256 dim x fp32 x n_splits workspace of <= a few MB); (b) FlashDecoding++'s unified-max partial softmax — pure arithmetic, removes the data dependency that forces the combine phase entirely; (c) the epilogue-side lesson of CODA/AttnQuantFusionPass in the only place it can apply here: the fused attention kernel should WRITE ITS FINAL OUTPUT in exactly the A-operand layout (fp16, row-major) Marlin's o_proj consumes, ending the fusion boundary at the Marlin door. Does NOT transfer: ClusterFusion/ClusterFusion++ tile-level attention->o_proj dataflow (needs thread-block clusters, sm_90+); FlashMLA/DeepGEMM (sm_80/sm_90 floors, TMA-era pipelining); CUTLASS 3.x EVT-on-TMA epilogues and warp-group ping-pong (sm_90). The literal research question — o_proj GEMM tiles consuming attention splits as they complete — does not port: Marlin's mainloop expects complete A rows, its W4A16 schedule and dequant pipeline are entangled with the tile schedule, and a splits-aware Marlin prologue is an engine-lane rewrite attacking a GEMM whose cost is weight streaming (a bandwidth lever this host falsified). The correct local shape of 'attention+projection fusion' is therefore fuse-walk-and-combine-into-one-kernel + output-layout contract, not producer/consumer GEMM tiling.

design.mechanism: Option A (in-kernel combine, primary): persistent walk kernel, ~72 CTAs (36 SMs x 2 per the occupancy law), each (seq,head,split) tile accumulates (m,l,acc) locally; on completion write partial to the L2-resident workspace, __threadfence(), atomicAdd(ctr[seq]); the last-arriving CTA per sequence LSE-merges siblings from L2 and emits the final fp16 rows directly in Marlin's expected layout. Deterministic if the combiner reads in fixed split order (semaphore semantics, not atomicAdd-on-floats — per CUTLASS discussion #317 tradeoff). Counter reset captured inside the graph. Option B (FlashDecoding++-style, no combine phase at all): fix per-head unified max M_h for the step (computed from the previous step's max plus a provably safe margin, per their sec on unified max selection), have every split emit exp(x - M_h) partial sums that are order-independent ATOMIC float accumulations into one buffer; the 'combine' degenerates to a division by the accumulated denominator, foldable into the first consumer. This removes the workspace round-trip AND the second launch AND the cross-split dependency chain in one move. Option C (Marlin prologue consuming splits): rejected — engine-lane rewrite, weight-stream-bound GEMM, falsified-bandwidth-lesson territory.
design.failure_modes: Option A: (1) replay safety — per-seq counters must reset in-graph or replay 2 deadlocks/double-merges; (2) occupancy — if register pressure (256-dim fp32 accumulator per head: tile over dims, e.g. 64-lane chunks, or spill to smem) drops CTAs/SM below 2 the walk gets slower, not faster; (3) conflicted STS halves when staging sibling partials through smem in the combiner — lay out banks explicitly; half2 staging already measured NO_DIFF in-engine, do not spend there; (4) keep split assignment fixed across steps for bitwise-comparable outputs (fp32 LSE math unchanged). Option B: numerics is the risk — unified max must bound the true max for the whole step or exp overflows / under-normalized weights appear; the paper's safe-max analysis covers it statistically but head_dim 256 long-ctx logit spread on this workload is [uncertain]; mitigation is their fallback re-normalization pass when the margin check trips. Option A/B shared: do NOT add KV prefetch depth to fund the fusion — KV pipelining measured NEGATIVE on this host; the win must come from the shorter dependency chain, not from more concurrency.
design.effort_estimate: Option A: kernel-lane 2-4 days (both kernels owned; cost sits in counter reset + ctx512/2048 x batch 4/8 sweep + bitwise comparison vs the split pair). Option B: kernel-lane 3-5 days plus a numerics battery (overflow margins across ctx sweep). Option C: culled at gate-1 (~10 min: the frame's own numbers — o_proj A-operand is B x 6144, bytes-trivial; the 4.3 ms is not an A-operand problem).
design.priority_signal: For: this is the one item whose mechanism names BOTH structural costs in the frame (workspace round-trip, second combine launch) and the strongest 2025-2026 published work (ClusterFusion, CODA, AttnQuantFusionPass) validates consumer-into-producer fusion as the live direction; FlashDecoding++ shows the softmax round-trip is removable with zero new hardware requirements — arch-independent, so no sm_90 excuse applies. Against: the published tile-fusion wins are all Hopper-cluster or training-stack results that do not port; the bytes involved (~0.12 ms of KV traffic, a <= few-MB workspace) are two orders below the multi-ms sensitivity floor, so the load-bearing question is whether the DEPENDENCY (launch boundary + LSE chain + per-step serialization) — not the traffic — is worth multi-ms at batch 4-8 [uncertain pending the #step-profile gap ledger]; if the 41.2-vs-50.1 gap is mostly walk-kernel occupancy instead, fusing the combine buys little and the item culls on the ledger.
